comparisons.peer_topic: Acquisition of ZT Systems: Agreement and Consideration
comparisons.peer_summary: On August 17, 2024, AMD agreed to acquire ZT Systems for approximately $4.9 billion, consisting of 8,335,852 shares of common stock and $3.4 billion in cash, with contingent consideration of up to 740,964 shares and $300 million payable upon meeting certain conditions.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom (AVGO) disclosed major completed or agreed-upon acquisitions in FY 2024 structured as cash-and-stock transactions to expand their respective infrastructure and computing capabilities. Broadcom acquired VMware for approximately $84.186 billion ($30.788 billion cash and $53.398 billion in stock) to enhance infrastructure software. Similarly, AMD entered into an agreement to acquire ZT Systems for approximately $4.9 billion (comprising $3.4 billion in cash and 8,335,852 shares of common stock) to support AI and general-purpose compute infrastructure for hyperscale computing. Both disclosures highlight the specific cash and stock components of the consideration paid.

sentences.text: The VMware stockholders received approximately $30,788 million in cash and 544 million shares of Broadcom common stock (on a split adjusted basis) with a fair value of $53,398 million.
We acquired VMware to enhance our infrastructure software capabilities.

On August 17, 2024, the Company entered into an agreement (the Agreement) to acquire ZT Group Int'l, Inc. (ZT Systems), a provider of AI and general purpose compute infrastructure for hyperscale computing companies, in a cash and stock transaction valued at approximately $4.9 billion (the Acquisition).
The aggregate closing consideration payable by the Company consists of 8,335,852 shares of the Company's common stock and $3.4 billion in cash.
